case.title: Hostinger-themed Cloudflare Pages phishing infrastructure
case.boundary: Exact code and content hashes support a Hostinger-themed credential-phishing software family. Naming shape and shared path grammar do not establish one operator, one provider account, victim count or Hostinger compromise.

nodes.label: 30 public scans across 25 task domains
nodes.meaning: The local Observatory subset supplied the initial Hostinger-themed Pages cluster. Scan observations are collection events, not victims or deliveries.

nodes.label: Exact credential-harvester code reuse
nodes.meaning: One exact JavaScript SHA-256 reads login fields and prepares credential-bearing POST requests. Byte identity supports software lineage, not human attribution.

nodes.label: 298 task names and 299-name family union
nodes.meaning: The exact task query returns 298 names. One additional matching name appears only as a final page behind a short link.

nodes.label: Automated deployment-name randomization
nodes.meaning: Fixed length, full alphabet coverage, uniqueness and near-maximum character entropy support automated project naming. The generator implementation and future names remain unknown.

nodes.label: Five exact live documents in an eight-host sample
nodes.meaning: A deterministic non-random check found five exact documents, two Cloudflare warning interstitials and one Cloudflare 522 response. The result cannot estimate family-wide uptime.

nodes.label: Zero valid archives from 25 fixed candidate paths
nodes.meaning: A later hash-gated check returned HTML for every fixed archive candidate. This is a narrow negative result, not proof that no kit archive existed elsewhere.

nodes.label: 67 same-shape domains across 12 lure prefixes
nodes.meaning: A partial preselected corpus shares a 24-letter naming shape and path grammar. The exact Hostinger harvester did not cross brands in the saved set.

nodes.label: Operator, victims and provider-account linkage unknown
nodes.meaning: Public scans and shared hosting cannot identify a human operator, prove one Cloudflare account, measure successful submissions or show Hostinger system compromise.

edges.note: Observed distribution supports automation but does not reveal the generator implementation or seed.
The preselected corpus supports contextual comparison only and is not a prevalence sample.
Descriptive hostname statistics cannot identify a human operator or provider account.
Similar naming shape and path grammar did not include exact Hostinger-core reuse in the saved partial corpus.
The deterministic eight-host sample cannot estimate family-wide uptime or campaign prevalence.
